sites.evidence_type: N-terminal HA epitope; parallel surface-display screen
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 607.8 ± 153.9 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)
sites.rationale: Experimentally validated N-terminal HA epitope insertion (after signal-peptide cleavage where present); surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in Tedman et al. deep receptor scanning.

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: FACS surface-expression assay: tagged OR2T11 reached the plasma membrane; antagonist treatment enhanced surface expression, indicating the receptor is functional enough to respond to ligands. No agonist-induced cAMP/calcium signaling assay for the tagged construct is reported.
sites.rationale: OR2T11 is a class-A GPCR (olfactory receptor) with an extracellular N-terminus spanning residues 1–20 and no signal peptide (topology string shows 'O' from position 1). The paper states the Rho-tag is placed 'at the N-terminus' of the full-length receptor but names no specific residue; because exactly one extracellular terminus exists at the N-terminal end, the junction is unambiguously a prepend (insert_after_residue = 0, residue_after = M at position 1). Python inspection confirms residue 1 = M and TM1 begins at residue 21, placing the prepend ≥20 residues from any TM boundary, well within the ≥3-residue constraint. Full-length human OR2T11 was cloned into pCI with a rhodopsin tag (Rho-tag) at the N-terminus to enhance plasma membrane localization; cell surface expression of the tagged receptor was confirmed by FACS, and antagonist treatment further enhanced surface levels.

sources.claim: The open reading frames of the mouse Or11g7 and human OR2T11 genes were cloned from the mouse or human genome, respectively, and subcloned into pCI (Promega, Madison, WI, USA) with a rhodopsin tag (Rho-tag) at the N-terminus, which has been previously demonstrated to enhance the plasma membrane localization of multiple ORs [ 63 ].

literature_notes: Only two ledger lines are available (L1, L2), both from the same publication (PMC11855683) and both describing the same N-terminal Rho-tag construct. L2 corroborates L1 by confirming FACS-measured surface expression of the tagged receptor. No ledger evidence supports insertions in any of the four extracellular loops (ECL1: 77–94, ECL2: 162–193, ECL3: 254–270) or at the C-terminus (intracellular, residues 288–316). The C-terminus is intracellular and therefore excluded from surface sites. No transposon, FP-fusion, or domain-insertion screen data are present in the ledger for this protein.
